prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and dynamics of a mass point, Newton's axioms, work, energy, conservation laws of mechanics)
Optics (geometric optics, light as electromagnetic wave, refraction and dispersion)
Oscillations and waves (harmonic oscillation, undamped, damped and forced oscillation, resonance, wave equation, superposition principle, interference, standing wave, reflection, refraction)
Static and dynamic fluids (pressure, density, buoyancy, pressure distribution, continuity equation, flow types, Bernoulli equation)

Electrical engineering (charge, electric field, electric field strength, potential, voltage, current, magnetic field, magnetic flux density, Lorentz force, induction law, coil, Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's rules, basics of AC theory)
Knowledge of basic electronic components as well as the designation and measurement of electrical quantities
Basics of measurement technology (transducer elements, bridge and amplifier circuits, multimeters, oscilloscopes, measurement signal processing and error analysis)

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have an overview of the most important sensor types and understand the essential principles of their physical functioning.
Students will have a basic knowledge of the methodical combination of physics, micromechanics, and electronics in sensor development.
Students will be able to apply and design suitable sensor systems in relation to practical problems, especially in the area of energy generation and efficient use.

syllabus_topics: Sensors: terms, overview of usable effects, application and selection
Functionality and application of selected sensors, especially in the field of generation and use of regenerative energies, e.g.
Sensors: for position detection as well as for detection of mechanical and fluidic quantities
Sensors for detecting distances and angles
Detection of chemical and biological material quantities of fluidic quantities
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
